facts.raw_span: crusting, irritation, and recurrent sinus infections for the past 5 years
denied hemoptysis, dyspnea, fatigue, or weight loss
no prior sinus surgeries or history of nasal trauma were reported
occasional use of nasal irrigation with tap water
destruction of the septal cartilage and turbinates, along with purulent, yellow drainage and crusting
C-reactive protein, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, angiotensin-converting enzyme, white blood cell count, and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody panel results were normal
HIV test was negative
substantial septal deformity with near complete destruction of the sinus septate
thinning of the posterior wall of the frontal sinuses, erosion of the bone near the right lacrimal system
enlarged lymph nodes in the mediastinum
sinus mucosa showed noncaseating granulomas
AFB PCR probe of hilar lymph node was positive

concepts.why: The presence of noncaseating granulomas, destruction of the septal cartilage and turbinates, and erosion of the bone near the right lacrimal system support this diagnosis
The patient's history of recurrent sinus infections and the presence of purulent drainage support this diagnosis
The presence of noncaseating granulomas and enlarged lymph nodes in the mediastinum support this diagnosis
The positive AFB PCR probe of hilar lymph node supports this diagnosis
The erosion of the bone near the right lacrimal system and the patient's age support this diagnosis
The presence of Staphylococcus aureus in the culture supports this diagnosis
The presence of Pseudomonas in the culture supports this diagnosis
The patient's history of recurrent infections and the negative HIV test support this diagnosis
The substantial septal deformity with near complete destruction of the sinus septate is consistent with the nasal and sinus destruction seen in Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis.

rationales.F01: Recurrent sinus infections suggest chronic sinusitis or an underlying condition like Wegener's Granulomatosis.
rationales.F05: Destruction of the septal cartilage and turbinates, along with purulent drainage, is indicative of a severe sinus infection or granulomatous disease.
rationales.F10: Enlarged lymph nodes in the mediastinum could be seen in conditions like sarcoidosis or tuberculosis.
rationales.F11: Noncaseating granulomas in the sinus mucosa are characteristic of conditions like sarcoidosis or Wegener's Granulomatosis.
rationales.F12: Positive AFB PCR probe is highly suggestive of tuberculosis.
